title: What is CLR, CTS, and CLS in .NET?
description: Understand the core components of the .NET runtime.

data.text: **Question:** What is CLR, CTS, and CLS in .NET?

CLR (Common Language Runtime) is the execution engine. CTS (Common Type System) defines how types are declared and used. CLS (Common Language Specification) is a subset of CTS that ensures language interoperability.

**CLR (Common Language Runtime):**
- Execution engine for .NET applications
- Provides memory management (GC)
- Handles JIT compilation
- Provides security and exception handling
- Equivalent to Java Virtual Machine (JVM)

**CTS (Common Type System):**
- Defines how types are declared and used
- Ensures all .NET languages share the same type system
- Types include classes, structs, interfaces, delegates, enums
- Supports value types and reference types

**CLS (Common Language Specification):**
- Subset of CTS for language interoperability
- Rules that .NET languages must follow
- Ensures code written in one language can be used by another
- Example: CLS-compliant code avoids unsigned integers
